page.text:
The real number system $\mathbb{R}$ completes the discrete rational
numbers $\mathbb{Q}$ into an unbroken geometric continuum. While
$\mathbb{Q}$ contains innumerable incommensurable 'holes'—such as
$\sqrt{2}$, $\pi$, and $e$—the real numbers fill every void, forming the
foundational stage for all of classical analysis.

Axiomatically, $\mathbb{R}$ is uniquely characterized up to
order-isomorphism as a *complete Archimedean ordered field*. The decisive
axiom distinguishing $\mathbb{R}$ from $\mathbb{Q}$ is the *Least Upper
Bound Property* (Dedekind completeness): every nonempty subset of
$\mathbb{R}$ that is bounded above possesses a supremum (least upper
bound) in $\mathbb{R}$.
